affordance_in_statement: If a valid assignment can be made, output ... the lexicographically smallest valid configuration (comparing the tier of module 1 first, then module 2, and so on).
removal_suggestion: Keep the lexicographic output requirement, but present the scenario as having module labels deliberately permuted into a worst-case search order, explicitly stating that committing colors for modules 1, 2, ..., n—even with ascending colors or simple local forward checking—causes exponential exploration on the supplied maximum-size cases.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Allocates arrays of size `1 << n`; with n up to 40 this requires infeasible memory and exponential time, and its DP state does not provide a viable 3-coloring algorithm.

recommended_edit: Add a scenario-level warning that the module numbering is an adversarial permutation: every maximum-size instance is selected so that any solver that commits modules in increasing numerical order, including lexicographic DFS with ascending tiers and basic local propagation, explores exponentially many partial assignments. State that the lexicographically smallest answer must be obtained by a more global coloring method rather than by enumerating prefixes.
regression_risk: This may not defeat a solver that already uses a genuinely strong graph-coloring algorithm or dynamic variable ordering; it should not restore glm-5 because its 2^n DP remains infeasible.
